title: Immune and Microcirculatory Pathways Associated with perioperative organ dysfunction
summary:
Surgical procedures can trigger immune and inflammatory responses in the body, which may impair blood flow through the smallest blood vessels and contribute to dysfunction of various organs. However, it remains largely unclear how these changes are related and to what extent they are influenced by the type and extent of surgery.

The aim of this study is to investigate the body's immune response during and after different surgical procedures and to identify potential associations with changes in blood circulation, organ function, and postoperative recovery.

A total of 150 adult patients undergoing one of six different types of planned surgical procedures will be included. Blood samples will be collected repeatedly before, during, and after surgery. In addition, blood flow through the smallest blood vessels beneath the tongue and at the fingernail will be examined using specialized cameras. These examinations will be performed up to 48 hours after the start of surgery. Furthermore, the function of various organs, mobility, well-being, and cognitive abilities will be assessed through blood tests and standardized questionnaires until the fourth day after surgery.

The collected data will be analyzed together and integrated into a computer-based representation of each patient's individual clinical course. This approach aims to improve our understanding of the relationships between the body's immune response, blood circulation, and recovery after surgery. In the long term, these findings may help to better understand the causes of postoperative complications and improve their early detection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who are capable of understanding the nature, scope, and potential consequences of the clinical study (capacity to provide informed consent).
Patients aged 18 years or older who are scheduled to undergo an elective procedure in one of the surgical categories listed above.
Before any study-specific procedures are performed, a written informed consent form must be signed and personally dated by the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Acute infections.
Chronic infections (e.g.,  hepatitis, HIV infections) or autoimmune diseases (rheumatoid arthritis) 
Congenital immunodeficiencies and treatment with immunosuppressive agents.
Participation in other clinical studies during the present study or within one month prior to study enrollment, or within at least five half-lives of the respective investigational medicinal product prior to study enrollment, whichever period is longer.
Medical or psychological conditions that prevent the proper conduct of the clinical study and preclude the signing of the informed consent form.
Insufficient German language proficiency to allow adequate and valid completion of the planned questionnaires and assessments.
Hemoglobin level (Hb) < 9 g/dL at the time of study enrollment.
